chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Red Allen in the 1940 Goodman sextet
summary: Maxwell dines at Red Allen's home and hears his advice about keeping time.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But you know, those days there were so many musicians in New York. I think it was 1940, after Benny got out of the hospital he reorganized the sextet. And we had Allen in the band, who was sort of like a legendary character to me. And he

was very nice to me, invited me up to his home. You know, we had a good chicken dinner. He asked me what I liked and I told him I liked fried chicken, I didn't mean anything by it. Later years I learned that some people are sensitive about that. But that happened to be what I liked.

And he played his records for me and told me he had made 150 records, and that was five records more than Louis Armstrong had made. And he was sitting there with his son, he was talking to his son about it, and he said, you make your son practice keeping time. No matter how good you play, you've got to keep time. And I was sitting there listening, thinking about taking notes. I thought I could learn a few things here myself.
